From Crimea to Kaliningrad — Do Ukraine's latest strikes signal a broader campaign? In less than a week, Ukraine has destroyed a section of Russia's Crimean Bridge and sunk one of its newest warships off the coast of Libya, amid a series of reported attacks stretching from the Baltic to the Black and Mediterranean seas. But Ukraine's latest strikes raise the question of what escalation dominance Kyiv holds over Moscow, and whether it is now playing out at an opportune moment. "Kerch, Baltiysk, the Gulf of Finland, Benghazi: all of them are points on Russia's own military supply chain, and Ukraine has now shown it can hit every one of them within a single week," said Catarina Buchatskyi, Director of Analytics at the Serpens Center for International Security.
